source.title: Modeling the Influence of Data Structure on Learning in Neural Networks: The Hidden Manifold Model
source.authors: Sebastian Goldt; M. Mézard; Florent Krzakala; L. Zdeborová

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalisation/test error as hidden-layer width and training time vary, but it does not use an interpolation-threshold double-descent setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width and training-time results relevant to V1 and V2. It does not report a sweep over sample size near an interpolation threshold, or tests of effective complexity, noise/regularization dependence, or parameter-count recasting. The memorability experiments and cited results are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study does not test double descent. Its width and training-time results come from one-pass (online) SGD, where every sample is fresh, so there is no finite training set and no interpolation threshold. The image-data runs use tiny two-layer networks (K≤8 for sigmoidal, K≤24 for ReLU), far below the size needed to fit MNIST or CIFAR10. No result can show a peak at the interpolation threshold, an epoch-wise second descent, or more data hurting. Double descent appears only through a cited reference (Mei & Montanari) and a remark on overparameterised generalisation.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but misweighted. The authors' main conclusions are three: the hidden manifold model is a solvable generative model of structured data; a Gaussian Equivalence Property gives exact ODEs for online SGD in two-layer networks; and the HMM reproduces features of real-data learning (incremental learning via specialisation, easy and hard examples in memorisation). The CIFAR10 overtraining rise is only a side remark in Appendix D.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses online SGD and analytical dynamics for two-layer networks on a synthetic hidden-manifold teacher-student task, plus separate minibatch experiments on image datasets. It does not reproduce the original double-descent interpolation-threshold sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported learning curves differ across data setting and activation: CIFAR10 sigmoidal runs show an overtraining increase, while ReLU runs have greater run-to-run variability.

fits_no_version.finding: In online SGD on the hidden manifold model, asymptotic test error drops when width grows up to teacher width, then improves only slightly as width exceeds it (Fig. 7a). There is no peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Without a finite training set (online learning), student overparameterisation relative to the teacher gives monotone, small generalisation gains.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger two-layer networks first match smaller networks on a plateau, then specialise and do better. This holds on the HMM and on MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks learn functions of increasing complexity during training (incremental learning via specialisation).

fits_no_version.finding: For CIFAR10 with small sigmoidal networks, test error rises again after several epochs of plain SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinary epoch-wise overfitting in under-parameterised two-layer networks.

record.problems: The size and training-time curves are primarily presented in figures rather than as numerical tables. Several learning-curve observations use individual or representative runs; the ReLU runs are explicitly reported to have high run-to-run variability. The experiments do not locate an interpolation threshold.
record.rows_left_out: Memorability results in Fig. 9 and the corresponding text were left out because they measure per-image classification frequency after one epoch, not the claim's test-error curves over model size, epochs, or sample size. Other cited results were not entered as study results.

untested.parts: No width sweep reaching the size that interpolates a finite training set.
No training-time curves for models near or past interpolation, and no long training to look for a second descent.
Sample size is not varied near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep past interpolation in any model class.
No label-noise, multiple-peak or regularisation-tuning analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not one of the original sources. The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its V1/V2 labels should be dropped. Online learning removes the interpolation threshold that every double-descent version depends on, and the minibatch experiments use networks far too small to interpolate. All rows are re-linked to 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies hidden-layer width in two-layer networks, but does not locate a training-set interpolation threshold or test the claimed peak near that threshold in deep networks.
The paper measures error over training time, but does not locate an interpolation threshold over epochs or test a fall-rise-fall curve tied to that threshold.
Training sample size is not varied near an interpolation threshold.
No cross-model-class interpolation-point sweep is reported.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak locations.
The claimed noise, multiple-peak, and optimally tuned regularization effects are not tested.
The paper does not recast complexity using an effective parameter count.

rows.subject: two-layer sigmoidal student network
rows.operation_detail: Varied student hidden-layer width and measured asymptotic generalisation error.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicated two standard deviations over five runs.
rows.note: The text says adding hidden units improves performance when the student has fewer units than the teacher, and reports small improvements as student size increases beyond teacher size. It does not report an interpolation peak.
rows.check: Online SGD with infinite fresh data and K=Z·M hidden units for M=1 has no interpolation threshold, so it cannot show the V1 peak. The 'partial' state is unfounded. The small monotone gains beyond teacher width belong under fits_no_version.

rows.measure: generalisation error over training time and width
rows.note: The text describes an initial error decay to a plateau, followed by lower error for K>1 after further training; larger networks perform better. It does not report a size-wise interpolation peak or an epoch-wise fall-rise-fall.
rows.check: The Fig. 8(a) curves describe a plateau then specialisation in online learning with K=1–8. There is no finite training set and no interpolation threshold, so neither V1 nor V2 can be assessed.

conditions.value: hidden manifold model; delta=0.05, D=25, M=10

rows.note: The text describes initial decay and a plateau, followed by further improvement for larger students after about 10^3 epochs; it does not describe a fall-rise-fall trajectory.
rows.check: This duplicates r4 (same figure and setting). Online learning cannot show the epoch-wise double descent tied to an interpolation threshold. 'Absent' overstates what the measure can show.

rows.subject: two-layer sigmoidal networks
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean-squared error during training on MNIST odd-versus-even digit classification.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate two standard deviations in Fig. 8(b).
rows.note: The authors describe larger networks as first learning functions equivalent to smaller networks, with a plateau before specialisation. They do not describe fall-rise-fall error over epochs.
rows.check: MNIST with K≤8 sigmoidal units (about 6k parameters against 60k samples) is far below interpolation, a regime where V2 does not predict a peak. The curves can't show the V2 effect.

rows.subject: two-layer sigmoidal networks
rows.size_stated: increasing hidden-layer sizes; plotted widths include K=1, 2, 4, and 8
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean-squared error over training time on real image datasets.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars indicate one standard deviation in Fig. 10.
rows.locator: Fig. 10; Sec. V A; Appendix D
rows.note: The authors state that the datasets show learning of functions of increasing complexity. They also explicitly report that CIFAR10 generalisation error starts increasing after several epochs of overtraining; no later second descent is described.
rows.check: The CIFAR10 overtraining rise in small networks well below interpolation is ordinary overfitting. Training was not run long enough to look for a second descent, so V2 is not assessable. This belongs under fits_no_version.
